Definition: from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and στοίχος (an aim); to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth:--err, swerve.
BiblicalUsage: To miss the mark is to swerve from the truth, and Paul uses it three times for the same danger. Some turned aside to vain jangling, some erred concerning the faith by chasing what is falsely called science, and Hymenaeus and Philetus erred by saying the resurrection is past already.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the target is small and the pull is constant, and a little swerve at the start becomes a wide miss by the end. Holding the pattern of sound words is how a person stays on the mark, and I hold that the faith once delivered is worth aiming at with everything I have.
